tuned_on: the 2026-10-14 brainstorm experiment's own 57-doc dev split, not this tool's sha256(path) dev split (variant B was written after reading those dev errors, so only the holdout split is untouched by tuning)
note: Frozen. Any edit to this file, even a wording fix in a note, changes the sha256 every results row records; report refuses to pool rows across shas and gives a verdict only for results made under the current file. Ship an edit as a new frozen version with a new frozen_at, which restarts the holdout.
instructions: Which solution-doc category best fits the engineering lesson described in `lesson`? Pick the category whose description matches the main subject of the lesson.

security-issues.what: Vulnerabilities and hardening: injection, secrets or token leakage, unsafe parsing of untrusted input, permission or trust-boundary bypass, redaction.
security-issues.not_for: General shell or script bugs with no attacker or secret involved.

logic-errors.what: A concrete defect in program logic that produced wrong behavior: state-machine or parser bugs, stale or inconsistent state, off-by-one, race conditions, wrong exit codes, fail-open checks.
logic-errors.not_for: Authoring conventions, process advice, or CI and build configuration problems.

build-errors.what: Failures in the build, CI, packaging or test-runner toolchain: dependency resolution, schema or lint validators, bats or vitest quirks, tool version incompatibilities.
build-errors.not_for: Bugs in the plugin's own runtime logic.

integration-issues.what: Problems at the boundary with an external system: GitHub API, gh or gt CLI behavior, MCP servers, third-party CLIs, provider setup and cross-plugin wiring.
integration-issues.not_for: Pure internal logic bugs or style conventions.

code-quality.what: Authoring conventions, design patterns, anti-patterns and gotchas for writing agents, commands, skills, docs and shell; guidance and lessons that apply across many files. The default home for general engineering knowledge.
code-quality.not_for: A single concrete defect in one specific script or command.

workflow.what: How work flows through git and GitHub: branches, stacked PRs, merge queues, restacks, review and resolve loops, worktrees, release and changeset process, session and gate procedures.
workflow.not_for: The correctness of a single script's logic.

protocol.primary_metric: adjudicated accuracy on the holdout split (docs dated after frozen_at); printed as agreement until review marks exist
protocol.thresholds_note: Fixed in advance; never tuned on eval data.
protocol.decision_rule: No change ships without GO: NO-GO and INSUFFICIENT-DATA both keep the current Sonnet category table.

go_rule.test: paired non-inferiority, Tango score interval on Jev minus folder correctness over the same holdout docs
go_rule.look_note: One pre-registered look at 155 adjudicated holdout docs (about 80% power at 25% discordance). Earlier reports are descriptive only and print INSUFFICIENT-DATA.

adjudication.note: A random sample of agreements is judged too, to limit discrepant-analysis bias.
